# pixellab: commands, the stdio protocol and MCP

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs-cli.mjs from the command registry: run `npm run docs:cli` after changing a command. Don't edit by hand. -->

`pixellab` reads and edits the pixel art in a `.pixellab` document and publishes it as the SVGs a site inlines. It has three doors onto one command registry (`cli/lib/registry.mjs`): the command line, `pixellab serve --stdio` for the Mac app, and `pixellab serve --mcp` for agents. Every command takes the same params (a JSON Schema object) and returns the same JSON through each door.

- [Commands](#commands)
- [The command line](#the-command-line)
- [The stdio protocol](#the-stdio-protocol) (`serve --stdio`, for the Mac app)
- [MCP](#mcp) (`serve --mcp`, for agents) and [setup for Claude Code](#setup-for-claude-code)

## The command line

```
pixellab <group> <verb> [args] [--flags] [--json] [--document <path.pixellab>]
```

The leading words name the command (`scene place` is `scene.place`; the longest match wins). Positionals fill the command's arguments in order; every param is also a `--kebab-case` flag. Booleans: `--flag`, `--no-flag`. Lists: comma-separated (`--at 14,6,1`) or the flag repeated; a list of pairs (pixels) is `3,4 5,6` or the flag repeated. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 command error (or `check` found problems), 2 usage error. With `--json`, errors are `{"error": {"code", "message", "details?"}}` on stderr.

| global flag | |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | print the command's result as JSON |
| `--document` | the .pixellab document (else $PIXELLAB_DOC, ~/.config/pixellab/config.json, or the document in --site) |
| `--site` | a site checkout holding the document (else $PIXELLAB_SITE, the config file, ~/Projects/jlawcordova.github.io) |
| `--out` | write the PNG of a render command to this file |
| `--dry-run` | an edit command shows what it would write (a diff) and writes nothing |
| `--force` | an edit command writes despite validation problems or a file changed on disk |
| `-h, --help` | help for the command or group |

**Edits are one-shot.** A command that edits a doc loads it, applies the edit, validates the doc with the engine, serializes it with the engine and writes it atomically (temp file and rename), then prints what changed and `wrote <file>`. It refuses, writing nothing, when the doc has validation problems (code `invalid`, the problems in `details`) or the file changed on disk while it ran (code `conflict`); `--force` writes anyway. `--dry-run` prints the unified diff it would write, any problems, and writes nothing. With `--json` the result gains `saved: [{ doc, file, wrote, hash }]` or `dryRun: [{ doc, file, diff, problems, conflict }]`. The `doc.*` commands (undo, redo, save…) only make sense in a session, so they run through `pixellab serve`.

The document comes from `--document`, else `PIXELLAB_DOC`, else `~/.config/pixellab/config.json` (`{"document": "…"}`), else `--site <checkout>` / `PIXELLAB_SITE` / `{"site": "…"}` (the `*.pixellab` under the site's `src/assets/pixel-art/`, or its legacy `source/` folder), else `~/Projects/jlawcordova.github.io`.

## The stdio protocol

`pixellab serve --stdio [--document <path> | --site <checkout>]` is the Mac app's server: newline-delimited [JSON-RPC 2.0](https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification) on stdin and stdout, one message per line. stdout carries nothing but JSON-RPC; logs go to stderr. Requests are answered one at a time, in order. Batches are not supported. Protocol version: 1 (`session.info` reports it).

The server holds a **session**: docs open as in-memory working copies with undo and redo (at most 200 steps; rapid repeats of the same edit within a second, such as a held arrow key or one paint stroke sent as many `object.paint` calls, merge into one step). Every command reads the working copies, so `scene.render` shows unsaved edits. Nothing is written until `doc.save`.

**Methods** are the command names (`scene.place`, `doc.undo`, … see the reference), plus:

| method | result |
| --- | --- |
| `session.info` | `{ name: "pixellab", version, protocol, pid, document: { root, name, kind, publishDir, siteRoot }, site, sourceDir, stateDir, saves: "direct", docs: [DocStatus] }` |
| `shutdown` | `{ ok: true }`, then the server stops reading and exits 0. It also exits when stdin closes. |

```json
→ {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"scene.place","params":{"name":"hero-island","object":"pine","at":[14,6,1]}}
← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"doc.changed","params":{"doc":"scene:hero-island","dirty":true,"canUndo":true,"canRedo":false}}
← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"doc":"scene:hero-island","changed":true,"summary":"pine placed at column 14, row 6, level 1","path":"198","item":{"object":"pine","at":{"tile":[14,6,1]}}}}
```

**Results** are the command's JSON. The shapes the app needs most:

- `scene.render` / `object.render`: `{ png, scale, viewBox: [x, y, w, h], width, height, time | frame, items: [{ path, object, at, id?, pose?, bounds: [x, y, w, h] }] }`. `png` is a base64 PNG with a transparent background at an integer `scale`; `bounds` are in output pixels (scale included), for hit-testing; `path` is the item's dotted path (`"5.2"`). An object render's item has `path: null` and the result has its `anchor`.
- Edits: `{ doc: "scene:<name>" | "object:<name>", changed, summary, ... }`; scene item edits add `path` (the item's path after the edit) and `item`; paint edits add `pixels` (how many changed).
- `DocStatus` (in `doc.changed`, `session.info` and `doc.status` without a doc): `{ doc, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }`. `doc.status` with a doc adds `file, exists, stale` (the file changed on disk since it was opened), `undo: [edit summaries]`, `redo: [...]` and `proposal?`.
- `doc.save`: `{ doc, file, wrote, hash, bytes, diff, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }` (`wrote` is false when the file already held exactly this text).
- `doc.undo` / `doc.redo` / `doc.revert`: `{ doc, changed, summary, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }`.

**Errors** are JSON-RPC errors with a stable `data.code`:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"scene.move: item is required","data":{"code":"usage","details":["item is required"]}}}
```

| `error.code` | when | `data.code` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| -32700 | a line that isn't JSON (`id` is null) | |
| -32600 | not a JSON-RPC 2.0 request | |
| -32601 | no such method | `not_found` |
| -32602 | bad params | `usage` (with `details`: every problem) |
| -32000 | the command ran and failed | `not_found`, `invalid` (validation problems in `details`), `conflict`, `dirty`, `exists`, `ambiguous`, `is_group`, `at_front`, `paint_blocked`, `color_cap`, `load_error`, … |
| -32603 | a bug | `internal` |

**Notifications** from the server (no `id`):

| method | params | when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `doc.changed` | `{ doc, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }` | after each edit, undo, redo, save, revert, and when a clean open doc reloads because its file changed. Sent before the request's response. |
| `files.changed` | `{ files: ["scenes/hero-island.mjs", …] }` | sources changed on disk (another editor, git, an applied proposal, a save), debounced 150 ms |
| `proposals.changed` | `{ proposals: [ProposalSummary] }` (as `proposal.list`) | a proposal was written, applied or rejected |
| `activity.appended` | `{ entries: [{ time, tool, args, ok, summary }] }` | an MCP server logged tool calls |

An open doc without unsaved changes reloads from disk when its file changes; one with unsaved changes stays as it is, `doc.status` reports it `stale`, and its `doc.save` fails with `conflict` until it's reverted or saved with `force`.

## MCP

`pixellab serve --mcp [--direct] [--document <path> | --site <checkout>]` is an MCP server over stdio (protocol `2025-06-18`, hand-written: `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`). Tools are the commands with `.` → `_` (`scene.place` → `scene_place`), each with its params as `inputSchema`. A tool's result is `content: [{ type: "text", text: <the result as JSON> }]` plus `structuredContent` (the result); render tools return the PNG as an `image` content block first, so agents can see the art. A failed command is a result with `isError: true` and `structuredContent: { error: { code, message, details? } }`; an unknown tool is a JSON-RPC error.

**Agents propose, people approve.** Edits stay in the server's session. `doc_save` validates the doc (refusing one with problems unless `force`) and writes a **proposal** to the state dir instead of the document; a person approves it in Pixel Lab's Agent window or with `pixellab proposal apply`. With `--direct`, `doc_save` writes the document instead. Left out of the tools: `proposal_apply` (approving a proposal is for a person, in Pixel Lab or with pixellab proposal apply); `proposal_reject` (rejecting a proposal is for a person); `art_build` (it publishes the SVGs a site inlines; a person publishes after approving); `document_copy` (saving a copy of the document is for a person). With `--direct`, `art_build` is a tool.

### Setup for Claude Code

With the app installed by `scripts/install.sh`, point Claude Code at the CLI inside it (the Agent window's Connect row shows the same command):

```sh
claude mcp add pixellab -- node "$HOME/Applications/Pixel Lab.app/Contents/Resources/cli/bin/pixellab.mjs" serve --mcp
```

Or at this repo's CLI, for development:

```sh
claude mcp add pixellab -- node /Users/jlawcordova/Projects/jlawcordova-lab/cli/bin/pixellab.mjs serve --mcp
```

Add `--document <path.pixellab>` (or `--site <checkout>`) after `--mcp` for another document, or set `PIXELLAB_DOC`. Proposals land in the state dir for review; run `pixellab proposal list` and `pixellab proposal show <id>` to see them from a terminal.

## Proposals and activity

The state dir is `$PIXELLAB_STATE`, else `~/Library/Application Support/Pixel Lab/`.

- `proposals/<id>.json`: `{ id, doc: "scene:<name>" | "object:<name>", baseHash, source, summary, createdAt, agent }`. `id` is `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-xxxxxx` (UTC, sortable). `baseHash` is the sha256 (hex) of the file the agent opened, or null for a new doc. `source` is the full new file, serialized by the engine. `summary` lists the edits since the doc was opened. `agent` is the MCP client's name and version. Saving the same doc again in one MCP session rewrites its proposal.
- `activity.jsonl`: one line per MCP `tools/call`: `{ time, tool, args, ok, summary }` (`tool` is the MCP tool name).

`proposal.apply` refuses (`conflict`) when the file no longer has `baseHash`, and (`invalid`) when the proposed doc has validation problems, unless forced; then it writes `source`, deletes the proposal, and reloads an open, unchanged working copy. `proposal.reject` deletes it. `proposal.render` renders the proposed doc over the files on disk (the shape of `scene.render` or `object.render`) without writing, for the Agent window's ghost preview.

## Command reference

### activity

#### activity.list

The last MCP tool calls agents made, oldest first.

```
pixellab activity list [--limit <n>]
```

Each entry is { time, tool, args, ok, summary }, from activity.jsonl in the state dir.

read-only · MCP tool `activity_list`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--limit` | integer | default `50` | how many entries (1 to 1000) |

### art

#### art.build

Publish: validate every source, compile each scene with an output and write the SVGs.

```
pixellab art build [--dir <text>]
```

Validates the document's files on disk (unsaved working copies aren't in it; unsaved lists them), renders each scene with an `output` to a rect SVG, merges each color group into one <path>, checks the result lossless and within its budget (100 KB raw / 25 KB gzip, or the manifest's), and writes <publish dir>/<output>. The publish folder is the manifest's publish.dir (relative to the document), or --dir; with neither it refuses. Nothing is written when any source has a problem. Returns { ok, publishDir, outputs: [{ file, scene, raw, gzip, over, report }], previewOnly: [{ scene, raw, gzip, over, report }], problems, ms, unsaved }.

read-only · writes files directly · not an MCP tool

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dir` | string |  | the folder to write the SVGs to (else the manifest's publish.dir) |

```sh
pixellab art build
pixellab art build --dir ~/Desktop/art
```

#### art.preview

Render the review PNG of an object (standing on a tile) or a scene, on the card color; `palette` for the swatch sheet.

```
pixellab art preview <name> [--scale <n>] [--kind <object|scene>] [--out <file.png>]
```

The picture an agent or a person checks art by: an object on one 32×16 tile outline, a scene at its viewBox (first variant, frame 0), both on the document's card color (manifest preview.card). Refuses (code invalid) when the doc or what it uses has problems. Returns { name, kind, scale, width, height, png } with the PNG as base64; --out writes it.

read-only · MCP tool `art_preview`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string | required | an object or scene (or objects/<name>, scenes/<name>), or palette |
| `--scale` | integer | default `1` | whole-pixel zoom of the PNG (1 to 16) |
| `--kind` | `object` \| `scene` |  | which kind name is, when both exist |

```sh
pixellab art preview pine --scale 4 --out /tmp/pine@4x.png
pixellab art preview palette --out /tmp/palette.png
```

#### art.sizes

Bytes each object and each color adds to a compiled scene, against the document's git HEAD.

```
pixellab art sizes <name>
```

The bytes a compiled scene loses, raw and gzip, when an object's items are left out or a color's paths are dropped (costs overlap a little), now and as committed at HEAD of the repository the document is in. Returns { scene, output, now: { raw, gzip }, head: { raw, gzip } | { reason }, objects: [{ object, placed, raw, gzip, headRaw, headGzip }], colors: [{ color, raw, gzip, headRaw, headGzip }] }.

read-only · MCP tool `art_sizes`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string | required | a scene (or scenes/<name>) |

```sh
pixellab art sizes hero-island
```

### check

#### check

Validate the sources with the engine, all of them or one doc.

```
pixellab check [name] [--kind <object|scene>]
```

Problems are the engine's "<file>: <where>: <rule>" lines. With a name, only the problems in that doc and the files it uses (palette.mjs, the objects it places or extends) are listed. On the command line, the exit code is 1 when there are problems.

read-only · MCP tool `check`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string |  | an object or scene (or objects/<name>, scenes/<name>); every source when left out |
| `--kind` | `object` \| `scene` |  | which kind name is, when both exist |

```sh
pixellab check
pixellab check hero-island
pixellab check objects/pine --json
```

### doc

#### doc.close

Close an open doc (refused with unsaved changes unless --force).

```
pixellab doc close <doc> [--force]
```

read-only · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_close`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |
| `--force` | boolean | default `false` | drop unsaved changes |

#### doc.merge

Merge the changes to a doc's file on disk into its working copy, keeping the unsaved edits.

```
pixellab doc merge <doc>
```

A three-way line merge: the file as the doc was opened or last saved, the file now, and the working copy. One undo step; the doc stays dirty with its own edits. A doc with no unsaved edits just reloads. When both sides changed the same lines it refuses with code merge_conflict (details: [{ base: [from, to], ours: [lines], theirs: [lines] }]) and changes nothing. Returns { doc, merged, changed, summary, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }.

edits docs · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_merge`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |

#### doc.open

Open a scene or object as a working copy, with undo and redo.

```
pixellab doc open <doc>
```

Edits to an open doc stay in memory until doc.save. Editing a doc that isn't open opens it, so this is only needed to start from a clean status.

read-only · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_open`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |

#### doc.redo

Redo the last undone edit to an open doc.

```
pixellab doc redo <doc>
```

edits docs · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_redo`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |

#### doc.reload

Load an open doc from disk again, only if no unsaved work is lost.

```
pixellab doc reload <doc>
```

Reloads when the working copy has no edits its file lacks: it is clean, or it matches the file (as after its proposal was applied). Refuses with code dirty (details: the edits that would be lost) when there are unsaved edits, and with code proposed while its proposal waits for the owner. Returns { doc, reloaded, changed, summary, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }; reloaded is false when the doc already matched the file. doc.revert is the one that drops edits.

edits docs · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_reload`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |

#### doc.revert

Load an open doc from disk again, dropping its changes (as one undo step).

```
pixellab doc revert <doc>
```

A doc that was never saved (made by scene.new or object.new) is discarded. To reload without dropping anything, use doc.reload.

edits docs · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_revert`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |

#### doc.save

Save an open doc: validate, serialize with the engine and write its source (MCP: write a proposal).

```
pixellab doc save <doc> [--force]
```

Refuses a doc with validation problems (code invalid, details: the problems) and a file that changed on disk since the doc was opened (code conflict), unless --force. In the MCP server it writes a proposal to the state dir for a person to approve instead (unless started with --direct). Returns { doc, file, wrote, hash, diff, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }, or { doc, proposal, file, summary, edits, diff, warnings?, … } for a proposal: edits lists the edits since the doc last matched its file, and warnings says when Pixel Lab has the doc open with unsaved edits.

edits docs · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_save`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |
| `--force` | boolean | default `false` | save despite problems or a conflict |

#### doc.status

Whether open docs have unsaved changes, and can undo or redo.

```
pixellab doc status [doc]
```

With a doc: { doc, dirty, canUndo, canRedo, file, exists, stale, undo: [edits], redo: [edits], edits, proposal?, synced?, unsavedInApp }. stale: the file changed on disk since the doc was opened or last matched it. edits: the edits since the doc last matched its file (what a proposal lists). synced: how the doc was brought in line with disk after its proposal was applied or rejected ({ proposal, outcome, action }). unsavedInApp: Pixel Lab has this doc open with unsaved edits, so a proposal for it will clash with them. Without a doc: { docs: [{ doc, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }], unsavedInApp: [docs Pixel Lab has open with unsaved edits], settled: [proposals settled lately] }.

read-only · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_status`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string |  | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |

#### doc.undo

#### document.copy

root is the .pixellab folder (or a legacy source/ folder in a site checkout, kind legacy-site); from says how it was named (--document, --site, PIXELLAB_DOC, PIXELLAB_SITE, the config file or the default); publishDir is where art build writes (null when the manifest names none); then the git branch, and how many scenes, objects and colors it has, with the count of validation problems.

### proposal

#### proposal.apply

Apply a proposal: check its base, validate it, write the doc's source and remove the proposal.

```
pixellab proposal apply <id> [--force]
```

Refuses (code conflict) if the file changed since the proposal was made, and (code invalid) if the proposed doc has validation problems, unless --force. An open working copy of the doc with no unsaved edits reloads from the new file (reloaded: true); one with unsaved edits has the proposal merged into it, keeping them (merged: true), or, when both changed the same lines, stays as it is and is reported stale (conflict: true). The file is written either way.

edits docs · writes files directly · not an MCP tool

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (positional) | string | required | the proposal id (proposal.list) |
| `--force` | boolean | default `false` | apply despite a changed base or problems |

#### scene.place

```

Like the lab's Place tool: an item on a tile goes in back-to-front order (by row + col, then level, among the items on tiles), so it paints in front of what's behind it. pixellab scene set <name> <item> [--tile <n,…>] [--px <n,…>] [--col <n>] [--row <n>] [--level <n>] [--x <n>] [--y <n>] [--class <text>] [--id <text>]
```

--tile col,row,level or --px x,y place the item there (changing how it's placed if need be); --col, --row, --level (an item on a tile) and --x, --y (a pixel-placed item) set one coordinate, like the lab's Selected fields. --class sets the class list and --id the id; an empty value removes it. An id's motion track follows it when it's renamed and goes with it when it's removed. All in one undo step.

edits docs · MCP tool `scene_set`

| `--tile` | list of integer |  | a tile: col,row,level |
| `--px` | list of integer |  | a point in scene pixels: x,y |

```sh
pixellab scene set hero-island 0.0 --tile 3,4,0
pixellab scene set hero-island 0.0 --class 'sway slow'
```

#### scene.show

Show a scene's settings, size, objects and motion.

```
pixellab scene show <name> [--doc]
```

#### scene.snap

Snap a pixel-placed item to the level-0 tile under its placement point.

```
pixellab scene snap <name> <item>
```
